notes.title: Lovecraft inspirations in the media
notes.notes: [p]Born on August 20, 1890, during his lifetime, Lovecraft's stories were not widely known. However, over time, his work gained popularity and became firmly rooted in pop culture. This was undoubtedly influenced by numerous inspirations from the Cthulhu mythology.[/p][p][/p][p]Stephen King has mentioned more than once how Lovecraft's work frightened him in his youth. The king of horror hid many references to Lovecraft's work in his early writings. We can read about the book De Vermis in “Jerusalem's Lot” or the character Yog Soggoth in “Needful Things”. In comics, perhaps the most popular reference is the name of the psychiatric hospital from the Batman series - Arkham Asylum. In Lovecraft's stories, Arkham was the city where many of his works took place.[/p][p][/p][p]Moving on to cinema, the appearance of the aliens in the film “Alien” was heavily inspired by H. Giger's paintings depicting descriptions from the myths. Screenwriter Dan O'Bannon admitted that he drew a lot of inspiration from Lovecraft's work, including borrowing words and scenes, such as the discovery of the alien temple. Director John Carpenter, inspired by Lovecraftian horror, directed “In the Mouth of Madness” and “The Thing”.[/p][p][/p][p]However, we find by far the most references in games. From “Call of Cthulhu: Alone in the Dark” from 1981, through “Half Life”, “The Witcher” series and “Bloodborne”, Lovecraft continues to inspire. Not only large studios, but also small teams like us, Astrolabe Stories. We encourage you to check out our works: “Last Threshold” and the demo “Threshold of Awakening”.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/0b2e289bc98a411107ba4ebf61a0ce0a52492dc8.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: The sunken city R'lyeh
notes.notes: [p]Deep beneath the surface of the Pacific Ocean lies a sunken corpse-city. Built eons before recorded history, R'lyeh is the prison of the sleeping Cthulhu.[/p][p]The discovery of this place was described by the protagonist of one of Lovecraft's stories, Norwegian sailor Gustaf Johansen: “a coastline of mingled mud, ooze, and weedy Cyclopean masonry which can be nothing less than the tangible substance of earth's supreme terror—the nightmare corpse-city of R'lyeh... loathsomely redolent of spheres and dimensions apart from ours.”[/p][p]Furthermore, the city's architecture makes exploration and escape impossible. The structures are colossal and seem to be likened to non-Euclidean geometry - a system that deals with curved spaces rather than flat ones. In R'lyeh, changes in perspective can be observed, causing uncertainty as to what is vertical and what is horizontal.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/3b1fd83e8173e4462b0a1b4bfdc47b9b785e9be1.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Jane nad Jane Fonda
notes.notes: [p]We needed a good role model for Jane, our protagonist. So when it came to seeking inspiration for Jane, main character in our game we looked to her namesake. And so a renowned actress and activist, Jane Fonda, became our muse. As a homage to her, we included a creation Jane Fonda wore in one of her movies inside Jane’s closet.[/p][p][/p][p]Can you guess which one?[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/60ac696485f8d62c3aff1345e848bed16ca10e27.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Cthulhu - the most famous character from Lovecraft's myths
notes.notes: [p]The most famous character from H. P. Lovecraft's myths, Cthulhu, the Priest of the Ancient Ones, sleeps in the underwater city of R'lyeh. However, this does not mean that we are safe. The monster can haunt people in their dreams and cause nightmares. Thanks to this activity, it maintains the faith of its cult on Earth.[/p][p]It is described as a beast with an octopus head and a body with indistinct anthropoid shapes. In addition to a large number of tentacles, it also has sharp claws and dragon wings.[/p][p]When the planets align in the right position, Cthulhu will rise from its tomb at the bottom of the Pacific Ocean and destroy the world.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/219da25be782bd634ccd61f6dc7aa900d301ffc3.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Lovecraft inspiration in Treshold of Awakening
notes.notes: [p]Get to know what you are scared of, and then you will stop being afraid. Are you sure?[/p][p][/p][p]This simple principle has been completely profaned by H.P. Lovecraft. Cognition and knowledge here are not the way to tame evil - they lead to it. [/p][p][/p][p]One could say that cosmic horror is therefore anti-science by definition, although we, in creating the game Threshold of Awakening, prefer to read Lovecraft's intuitions differently. His grasp of horror touches most acutely that dark side of man, the realization that all the knowledge of this world pales beside the ghastly riddles of eternity... It is this aspect of the impossibility of knowing objective truth, the constant risk of madness that attracts us in the works of the loner from Providence. It is for this reason, that our heroine Jane must go to Tibet... What awaits her there is not only a struggle against the temptations of the Old Ones, but also against herself.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/d72382de81850ac332b603d2f94b8df9852a29ad.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Howard Phillips Lovecraft
notes.notes: [p]Known as the Father of Cosmic Horror. An American writer of horror, weird fiction, and fantasy, whose work has inspired many, including us—the members of the Astrolabe team.[/p][p]Howard Phillips Lovecraft was a loner who had been interested in astronomy since childhood. Unfortunately, he failed to get into his dream college major. Another long-standing passion of his was writing, in which he found greater luck. After writing to The Argosy newspaper, he was offered a job there. At the urging of a friend, he refined his stories, which were then published in The Vagrant and Weird Tales.[/p][p]The writer corresponded extensively with his readers and respected artists from across the country. Unfortunately, despite publishing many stories, Lovecraft struggled with financial problems for most of his life.[/p][p]He died of intestinal cancer in his hometown at the age of 47.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706643/468c80390b32971f61db485c7ad0e9f8aa4c714b.png"][/img][/p]
